title: An authored map of meaning-connections — the binary pole (antonym) and the condensed field (synonyms) of a term
note: A proxy carrying its provenance, not a real thesaurus. Each term records `antonyms` — the pole(s) it stands against, its binary structure (the compression: one bit, a fixed yes/no) — and `synonyms` / `associates` — the field of associated meaning condensed upon that bit (the relational, proportional, meant content a bit cannot hold). Connections are read symmetrically: a pole named one way holds both ways, so a bare opposite (noise against signal) need not be spelled out twice. Where a term is also a lexicon lexeme, its compounded ancestry (`defined_in_terms_of`) is read from the lexicon — language as the compounded creation of meaning over time. Bit-like terms (signal/noise, true/false, right/wrong) are the compression floor: a pole, no field. Condensed terms keep the bit and gather a field on it.
